hints: Searching the grid once per word repeats the same work: many words share the same start. How could you search for all words at the same time?
Build a trie of all words, then DFS from every cell while walking down the trie. If the current letters are not a prefix of any word, stop that path at once.

1. Insert every word into a trie; store the full word at its last node.
  2. From every cell, DFS with the trie root.
  3. Move to the child for the cell's letter; if missing, return.
  4. If that node holds a word, add it to the answer and clear it (no duplicates).
  5. Mark the cell with '#', visit the four neighbours, then restore the letter.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each word, run a separate word-search DFS from every cell.

approaches.name: Optimal: trie + backtracking DFS
approaches.idea: One DFS from each cell walks the grid and the trie together, so shared prefixes are explored once and dead prefixes are cut early.
approaches.time: O(R·C · 4·3<sup>L−1</sup>) worst case, plus O(total letters) to build the trie

explain: The board is dog / axo / ten. From the top-left d, the trie allows o (for dog) and a (for date): d→o→g finds dog, and d→a→t→e down the left column and along the bottom finds date. From the bottom-left t, t→e→n finds ten. goon fails because neither o next to the g has another o beside it, and cat dies at once since no cell is c. Clearing a word from the trie after finding it stops it being added twice.
recognize: Many words to find in one grid with up/down/left/right moves → trie of the words + backtracking DFS.
